subject: Post-demo: validate monthly burn bracket & PO approval path
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
To: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@orchard.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: validate monthly burn bracket & PO approval path

Thanks again for the demo this morning, Sam — appreciate you walking through the inference patterns for your search & summarization flows. I promised a short recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size the pilot and confirm procurement next steps.

Summary (quick):
- Workload: hybrid search + multi-turn summarization (avg context 1.5k tokens; occasional spikes to 6k).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~30 qps for search; summarization is bursty (30-60s windows).
- Goal: pilot to validate latency at 95th pct and cost per 1M tokens to inform 2027 run rate.

Questions / asks (please reply inline):
1) Monthly burn corridor: can you confirm the ballpark monthly token volume you expect during the pilot (low / expected / high)? We need this to size the reserved pool and recommend a commit band. Target ranges we typically use are: 10-50M, 50-250M, 250-1B+ tokens.
2) Unit economics target: do you have a target $/1M-tokens figure (or a max sticker that triggers escalation to procurement)?
3) Procurement gate: what is the PO/contracting threshold on your side that would require legal sign-off or an SOW (e.g., $25k/month PO vs $100k annual)? Any lead times to be aware of?

Attached: pilot proposal (v1) and a minimal token-econ workbook that shows estimated spend across three model variants. I put a conservative latency profile and a few quantization options we discussed.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the three numbers above by Wed (8/18).
- If the monthly band lands in the mid/high range, we prep a short SOW and loop Legal; if low, we can go CC/credit-card pilot.

Thanks — quick replies totally fine, we can iterate.

Best,
Irene
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-pilot-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf, 92KB); token-econ-workbook.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@orchard.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: validate monthly burn bracket & PO approval path

Irene — thanks, great summary. Inline answers below.

1) Monthly burn corridor: low 25M / expected 120M / high 420M tokens. Those are realistic for months 1-3 as feature ramp hits.
2) Unit econ target: ideally <= $40 per 1M tokens. Above $75/1M we need a stronger ops justification and will likely require exec review.
3) Procurement gate: anything above $60k total spend (monthly equivalent) needs a PO and legal review at Orchard; below that we can do a purchasing card for the pilot. Typical legal turnaround is 7-10 business days once they see draft SOW/PO.

I attached our internal forecast snapshot for context. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if it helps.

—Sam
Sam Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, OrchardAI
attachments: orchard-forecast-snippet.csv (csv, 18KB)

Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: validate monthly burn bracket & PO approval path

Sam — perfect, thanks for the clarity. A couple of follow-ups so we can finalize the recommender: 

- With expected = 120M and high 420M, we typically recommend a 3-month pilot with a commit band at the lower-mid point (we'd propose a 100-250M monthly commit band). That keeps latency SLAs affordable while giving you headroom for spikes. Does that band sit okay with Orchard?
- Based on your $/1M target ($40), our quick estimate (attached workbook) shows the following run rates for the pilot using M-variant quantized model: ~ $28/1M (40% quantized), $46/1M (mixed FP16), $80/1M (baseline FP32). We can lock a pricing tier that guarantees $/1M up to the chosen commit band.
- For procurement: if anything over $60k/month triggers PO/legal, we should prepare a short SOW and a purchasing path. Jordan — can you confirm typical Redwood PO minimums and legal SLA when we escalate? Karthik — any constraints on offer terms we should avoid to keep legal review light?

If Orchard is comfortable with the 100-250M recommendation, I'll draft a 1-page SOW + priced pilot quote and send to procurement for PO routing. If Orchard prefers CC pilot, we'll enable a credit-card onboarding flow and short-term overage protections.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: validate monthly burn bracket & PO approval path

Irene — quick confirmations:
- Redwood PO minimum for SOW-backed pilots is $30k total; most pilot SOWs we do are 3 months so that maps to ~$10k/mo floor. For reserved capacity / Dedicated we require a 3-month notice to provision if GPUs need allocation spikes; usually we can support short-term bursts but guaranteed SLA needs the commit.
- Legal SLA: for standard pilot SOW + our Master Services Addendum we can move in 3-7 business days for returning comments; complex security addenda (custom DPA/infosec questionnaires) add more time. For Orchard's $60k/month threshold, expect Legal to need a short SOW plus vendor intake — estimate 7-12 business days total.
- Offer terms: avoid bespoke IP clauses or long indemnity edits in the SOW; keep it to term length and MSA referencing. Karthik — I flagged the pricing tiers and the proposed $40/1M cap as reasonable; if they choose 100-250M commit we can lock the $35/1M rate for the 3-month pilot (subject to SOW).

I'll draft the one-pager SOW template and share it in Drive; Irene, once Sam confirms the band I'll populate finance rows and send to procurement.

Jordan
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
